topic: Wald-symmetry frontier for outcome-selected proximal synthetic-control roles. Fix two predeclared square donor/proxy partitions in a stationary geometrically beta-mixing panel with fixed moment, bridge-rank, positive ATT influence-variance, and nondegenerate ridge-loss-contrast margins. The treated unit has post outcome Y(0)+Delta and target tau=E Delta; every partition is a valid proximal bridge. Select between the roles using the same pre-period lambda=1 ridge loss and estimate the conventional proximal ATT. Under every bounded root-T selector gap, derive its selected-Gaussian limit and the exact symmetric-Wald coverage functional. Prove: exact selector ties protect every symmetric Wald level; coverage is nominal for every local gap iff the two standardized ATT statistics have equal squared correlations with the selector contrast; otherwise the strict coverage-error sign equals the gap sign times the squared-correlation difference. Realize both sides inside legal primitive proximal panels, including an open asymmetric family with strict undercoverage. Construct a corrected estimator using an early selector, a log-squared mixing gap, late bridge estimation, post residual averaging, and Bartlett HAC bandwidth N^(1/5); prove uniform selector-conditional studentized normality on the declared positive-variance class. Generic time splitting is supporting machinery, not novelty. Consumer: redesign the Shi et al. 2026 West-German proximal-SC role analysis as a predeclared two-candidate robustness analysis before retaining its negative GDP conclusion. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Independent derivation gives the binary selected-Gaussian coverage formula, exact nominal symmetric coverage at a zero selector gap, and all-gap validity iff the two standardized ATT statistics have equal squared correlations with the selector contrast. Exact Gaussian polynomial calculations reproduce both primitive covariance tables; the asymmetric legal proximal model yields 0.8858209104904335 coverage for a nominal 90 percent interval at standardized gap minus one, while the symmetric model has nonzero selected mean but exact two-sided coverage. A primitive local-array chart makes strict miscoverage open, and big-block Lyapunov plus Bartlett bounds vanish at the declared block and bandwidth rates. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Assemble the joint uniform Gaussian/HAC mapping lemma through singular joint covariances whose selector contrast and ATT marginals retain the stated positive variance margins. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce both exact covariance tables, exact tie coverage, and the 0.8858209105 asymmetric integral; pivot if the uniform mapping requires another model restriction or exact prior art contains the same proximal-role frontier. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_proxysplit_selection_inference.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For two predeclared valid donor/proxy partitions selected by smaller same-pre-period ridge loss, characterize the selected proximal-ATT limit and exact conventional symmetric-Wald coverage over every bounded root-T selector gap.

source_refs.claim: Proximal-SC theory predetermines donor and proxy roles; its German application assigns six controls as donors and ten as supplemental proxies without inference after data-driven role choice.
source_refs.author: Xu Shi, Kendrick Qijun Li, Myeonghun Yu, Wang Miao, Arun Kumar Kuchibhotla, Mengtong Hu, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Ignoring data-driven selection can invalidate conventional inference along local sequences near selection boundaries.
source_refs.author: Hannes Leeb and Benedikt M. Pötscher

source_refs.claim: Polyhedral conditioning yields exact Gaussian post-selection inference, but not unconditional conventional-Wald coverage for a role-selected proximal ATT.
source_refs.author: Jason D. Lee, Dennis L. Sun, Yuekai Sun, and Jonathan E. Taylor

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing proximal-SC theory fixes the donor/proxy partition, whereas same-sample loss selection turns the reported statistic near a loss tie into a coordinate chosen by a correlated Gaussian half-space event. Generic selective-inference work supplies conditional pivots, and synthetic-control inference fixes the specification; neither gives the unconditional two-sided conventional-Wald coverage functional or a necessary-and-sufficient condition for harmless role selection. The missing step is an exact half-space calculation indexed by both ATT statistics' correlations with the selector contrast, followed by realization of the admissible covariance geometries in primitive proximal panels.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A selected-Gaussian limit and exact coverage functional proving tie-level protection, all-gap nominality iff the standardized ATT statistics have equal squared selector correlations, the signed strict-error rule otherwise, and legal proximal-panel examples realizing both regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from the practical donor/proxy distinction through bridge identification and time-series ATT inference to the West-German application, then expose data-driven role choice as the unresolved inferential step.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Excluded controls can identify a donor bridge as proxies -> the donor/proxy partition changes construction and precision -> practitioners may prefer the better-fitting partition -> same-sample role choice creates a nonregular selected-ATT Wald problem

method_exemplars.technique: Represent selection as a Gaussian half-space or polyhedral event and integrate the conditional Gaussian law, adapting the proof to a selected coordinate of the joint ATT-loss-contrast limit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired coverage functional has the same Gaussian-linear selection geometry, but reports an unconditional symmetric interval rather than a conditional selective pivot.

method_exemplars.technique: Use long-panel projection expansions for average synthetic-control effects and propagate weight-estimation error into the ATT limit law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is an average post-treatment effect in a long panel, with the expansion stacked across two proximal constructions and coupled to their loss contrast.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish uniform selector-conditional inference for an early-role-selector, logarithmic-gap, late-bridge proximal synthetic-control estimator when the stacked Gaussian covariance may be singular but selector and ATT marginal variances remain positive.

source_refs.claim: The proximal-SC paper develops GMM and HAC inference for a predetermined donor/proxy partition, not conditional inference after a pre-period role selector.
source_refs.author: Xu Shi, Kendrick Qijun Li, Myeonghun Yu, Wang Miao, Arun Kumar Kuchibhotla, Mengtong Hu, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Separated-block sample splitting can remain asymptotically valid for beta-mixing triangular arrays when the target functional is sufficiently regular.
source_refs.author: Robert Lunde

source_refs.claim: Kernel HAC estimators are consistent under serial dependence and bandwidth restrictions, but the theory does not cover selector-conditional proximal estimators.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews

source_refs.excerpt: Its reproduced delta-method route uses post-transport to make yM_r^+B causal
no primitive learner class, rate derivation, or attainable example discharges it

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature supplies beta-mixing block separation, fixed-role proximal linearization, and HAC consistency only as separate components. The adjacent CausalSmith review independently exposes two relevant proof boundaries: its joint delta-method construction does not handle a discontinuous selector over changing lower-dimensional Gaussian supports, and a load-bearing variation rate is assumed without a primitive learner or attainable example. The first proof step needing replacement is full-covariance whitening or inversion: the argument must instead be uniform on a positive-semidefinite covariance class and operate only in the nondegenerate selector and ATT directions, while deriving the late bridge's product-rate remainder and Bartlett-HAC consistency from primitive mixing and rank conditions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform theorem showing that, conditional on either early-selected role, the late-block proximal ATT estimator studentized by Bartlett HAC converges to N(0,1) under explicit logarithmic-gap and N^(1/5)-bandwidth rates despite singular stacked covariances.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its proximal-SC estimand and panel notation, then isolate role selection as the reason predetermined-role HAC theory is insufficient.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fixed proximal bridges identify ATT -> analysts may compare credible role assignments by pre-period fit -> reusing that block contaminates Wald inference -> separated selection, bridge fitting, and post residual averaging should restore honest conditional inference

method_exemplars.technique: Couple beta-mixing blocks to independent copies across an expanding gap, then transfer a post-selection CLT conditionally on the training block.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The correction has the same dependent-data training/inference separation, with a proximal-GMM functional and uniform studentization as the new ingredients.

method_exemplars.technique: Control kernel-weighted sample autocovariances and truncation bias to prove consistency of Bartlett long-run variance estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested conditional limit theorem is studentized by a Bartlett HAC estimate of the selected post-residual influence process.

method_exemplars.technique: Linearize proximal synthetic-control bridge moments and propagate bridge-estimation remainders into a root-rate asymptotically normal ATT estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proximal ATT influence-function machinery must be localized to the late estimation block and then studentized conditionally on the earlier role choice.

open_problems.open_problem: For at least three predeclared valid donor/proxy partitions selected by minimum pre-period loss, characterize the multivariate selected-Gaussian Wald coverage function and the covariance geometry yielding nominal coverage for every local loss-gap vector.

source_refs.claim: Proximal synthetic control makes the donor/proxy partition a first-class modeling choice but assumes it is fixed before analysis.
source_refs.author: Xu Shi, Kendrick Qijun Li, Myeonghun Yu, Wang Miao, Arun Kumar Kuchibhotla, Mengtong Hu, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Simultaneous protection over all candidate models yields universally valid post-selection inference, usually with conservative critical values.
source_refs.author: Richard Berk, Lawrence Brown, Andreas Buja, Kai Zhang, and Linda Zhao

source_refs.claim: Dependent Gaussian approximation supports simultaneous confidence intervals for mean vectors without requiring nonsingular coordinate correlations.
source_refs.author: Danna Zhang and Wei Biao Wu

open_problems.why_unsolved: With multiple roles, the minimum-loss selector partitions the Gaussian limit into polyhedral cones and reports a different ATT coordinate on each cone. The binary equal-squared-correlation condition need not characterize global all-gap validity when ATT variances differ or the stacked covariance is singular. PoSI and max-statistic methods guarantee simultaneous protection but do not determine when the unadjusted role-specific interval is already exact, and the literature search found no multi-role proximal result linking conventional coverage to a necessary-and-sufficient covariance geometry.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A multivariate Gaussian cone-integral coverage formula, a necessary-and-sufficient covariance condition for nominal coverage at every local gap vector, and a feasible simultaneous or max-t correction with a dependent-panel limit theorem when that condition fails.

writing_exemplar.why: Its role-based proximal construction naturally motivates a menu of scientifically credible partitions rather than one arbitrary split.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Different excluded controls can serve as proximal proxies -> several predeclared assignments may identify the same ATT -> minimum-loss choice creates model uncertainty -> multi-role coverage geometry and a practical correction are needed

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose Gaussian space into polyhedral selection regions and calculate conditional laws of selected linear statistics.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Minimum-loss choice among multiple locally separated criteria becomes a collection of linear Gaussian inequalities.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert arbitrary post-selection coverage into simultaneous coverage over the candidate family and calibrate a common critical value.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Simultaneous intervals over all role-specific ATT estimators are the natural uniformly valid fallback when conventional selected intervals fail.

method_exemplars.technique: Approximate maxima of dependent vector sums by Gaussian maxima and consistently estimate their long-run covariance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A corrected multi-role interval requires a dependent-data max statistic valid under strong correlation or singular covariance across roles.

open_problems.open_problem: Among several valid donor/proxy partitions for the same proximal synthetic-control ATT, identify and estimate the role minimizing long-run ATT variance while retaining uniform inference at local variance ties.

source_refs.claim: The proximal-SC construction permits excluded controls to serve as proxies but does not characterize an efficiency-optimal donor/proxy allocation.
source_refs.author: Xu Shi, Kendrick Qijun Li, Myeonghun Yu, Wang Miao, Arun Kumar Kuchibhotla, Mengtong Hu, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: When many bridge functions identify one panel effect, regularization can target a minimal bridge and deliver root-rate inference, but it does not optimize across donor/proxy assignments.
source_refs.author: Guido Imbens, Nathan Kallus, and Xiaojie Mao

source_refs.claim: Semiparametric proximal theory characterizes efficiency bounds and locally efficient estimators under a fixed proxy structure.
source_refs.author: Yifan Cui, Hongming Pu, Xu Shi, Wang Miao, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Minimal-bridge regularization addresses multiplicity inside a fixed moment system, and semiparametric proximal theory optimizes inside a fixed proxy structure; neither compares the distinct influence functions produced by swapping controls between donor and proxy roles. The population-optimal role depends on role-specific bridge Jacobians and long-run covariance, making its estimated argmin nonregular near variance ties. The first proof step that fails is the fixed-model efficiency projection: it must be replaced by a finite collection of dependent influence functions and a selector or aggregator whose risk and coverage remain uniform near ties.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Role-specific proximal-ATT influence functions and long-run variances, a characterization of the variance-minimizing role, and either a separated selector with uniform oracle-risk and studentized-limit guarantees or a smooth aggregator with an explicit asymptotic variance bound at local ties.

writing_exemplar.why: Retain its practical framing of controls as interchangeable raw material for donor and proxy roles, then turn that flexibility into an efficiency-design question.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Controls can be assigned to donor or supplemental-proxy roles -> several assignments may identify ATT -> their Jacobians and residual processes imply different precision -> role allocation should target efficiency without invalid inference at near ties

method_exemplars.technique: Derive proximal influence functions by pathwise differentiation and project onto the fixed-model tangent space to obtain efficiency bounds and locally efficient estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Role-specific efficiency comparison requires these influence-function and efficiency-bound calculations before optimization across partitions.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit equivalence of multiple bridge solutions for the causal target and regularize toward a canonical minimal bridge while controlling the estimation remainder.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The role problem likewise has multiple valid representations of one effect, but the canonical choice is determined by ATT long-run variance rather than bridge norm.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine outcome-bridge and weighting-bridge moments into a doubly robust root-rate ATT estimator and derive its normal limit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its estimating equations provide a richer candidate influence-function class in which role-dependent efficiency can be compared.

open_problems.open_problem: When either candidate donor/proxy partition may violate proxy exclusion by a bounded amount, derive sharp proximal synthetic-control ATT sensitivity bounds and a selection-robust confidence region after minimum-loss role choice.

source_refs.claim: Proximal-SC identification requires predetermined proxies satisfying conditional exclusion and corresponding error-independence restrictions.
source_refs.author: Xu Shi, Kendrick Qijun Li, Myeonghun Yu, Wang Miao, Arun Kumar Kuchibhotla, Mengtong Hu, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Adaptive proximal inference allows some invalid proxies in a canonical linear point-treatment model, but not time-series donor/proxy role switching.
source_refs.author: Prabrisha Rakshit, Xu Shi, and Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen

source_refs.claim: Donor-selection methods detect possible spillovers and bound bias from donor misclassification while reusing excluded donors as proximal information.
source_refs.author: Michael O'Riordan and Ciarán M. Gilligan-Lee

open_problems.why_unsolved: Swapping a control between donor and proxy roles changes which exclusion restriction is required, so uncertain role validity is not ordinary coefficient misspecification. Existing invalid-proxy work treats an i.i.d. point-treatment system, while donor-spillover work studies bias sensitivity; neither combines bounded role-specific violations, bridge-rank restrictions, serial dependence, and pre-period loss selection. The unresolved mathematical obstacle is a sharp optimization over two perturbed bridge systems whose endpoint inference must remain valid across a nonregular selector boundary.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp ATT identified set under explicit bounds on each role's proximal exclusion moments, a computable endpoint representation for two square partitions, and a uniformly valid confidence region for those endpoints after pre-period loss selection.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from stringent proxy exclusions to practical proxy invalidity and then a formally protected causal target, moving the destination to dependent proximal synthetic-control roles.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Proximal identification relies on valid proxy exclusions -> candidate controls may violate them or experience spillovers -> role assignment changes which violations matter -> bounded-violation ATT regions must account for role uncertainty and selection

method_exemplars.technique: Translate proxy invalidity into direct-effect terms in proximal moment equations and separate causal and violation components using structural restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The sensitivity region likewise augments proximal bridge moments by explicit exclusion-violation terms, replacing sparsity with bounded deviations.

method_exemplars.technique: Bound causal-estimate bias under donor misclassification and reuse excluded donors as proximal information.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly connects donor validity, spillover contamination, and proximal reuse of excluded controls—the primitives altered by role reversal.

method_exemplars.technique: Stack proximal outcome and weighting moments, derive a doubly robust influence function, and establish ATT asymptotic normality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Endpoint inference can perturb these moments over the bounded-violation set and propagate their dependent influence processes.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize whether target-pre-span is redundant under post-transport, and whether it can instead replace post-transport, in causal spectral or proximal synthetic-control identification.

source_refs.excerpt: post-transport to make yM_r^+B causal but never uses target-pre-span

open_problems.why_unsolved: The adjacent reviewer identifies a precise assumption/proof mismatch: post-transport alone makes the displayed yM_r^+B object causal, while target-pre-span is unused. Carrying both assumptions into role-selected proximal constructions obscures whether role validity is structural or merely algebraic. The first proof step requiring revision is the causal interpretation of yM_r^+B after replacing post-transport by an equality derived from target-pre-span; if that implication fails, a legal-panel counterexample must delimit the two assumption classes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient transport characterization, or paired legal-panel counterexamples, separating regimes where post-transport suffices, target-pre-span substitutes for it, and neither condition identifies the proximal ATT.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its explicit bridge-identification assumptions and separation of donors from supplemental proxies to frame why a minimal structural condition matters.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Proximal synthetic control needs a bridge with causal interpretation -> spectral constructions may impose both span and transport assumptions -> an existing proof uses only transport -> the exact logical frontier between the assumptions must be characterized

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze equivalence classes of bridge solutions and prove when different bridge representations identify the same causal panel functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result asks whether two structural routes yield the same causal bridge functional or instead support different identified regimes.

literature_map:
Shi et al. (2026, JASA, arXiv:2108.13935) establish proximal synthetic-control identification and HAC/GMM inference with predetermined donor and proxy roles.
Their West-German application assigns six countries receiving nonzero SCPI weights as donors and the remaining ten as supplemental proxies, making the role choice consequential for the reported negative GDP effect.
Miao, Geng, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2018, Biometrika, arXiv:1609.08816) provide foundational rank and completeness logic for identification with two proxy types.
Cui et al. (2024, JASA, arXiv:2011.08411) derive proximal ATT influence functions, efficiency bounds, and locally efficient or doubly robust estimators for a fixed proxy structure.
Qiu et al. (2024, Biometrics, arXiv:2210.02014) bring weighting and doubly robust proximal formulas into synthetic control without studying data-selected roles.
Imbens, Kallus, and Mao (2021, arXiv:2108.03849) show that many bridge functions may identify one panel effect and regularize toward a minimal bridge; multiplicity across role partitions remains untreated.
Rakshit, Shi, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2025, arXiv:2507.19623) address some invalid proxies in a linear i.i.d. proximal model, identifying a nearby but distinct validity-selection frontier.
O'Riordan and Gilligan-Lee (2024, arXiv:2406.11399) detect spillover-contaminated donors and bound misclassification bias, but do not derive post-role-selection proximal Wald inference.
Li (2020, JASA) derives long-panel synthetic-control average-effect limits and valid subsampling, emphasizing that ordinary bootstrap inference may fail even without role selection.
Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021, JASA, arXiv:1912.07120) separate weight-estimation and post-outcome uncertainty and extend prediction intervals to beta-mixing series while fixing the SC specification.
Chernozhukov, Wüthrich, and Zhu (2021, JASA, arXiv:1712.09089) provide conformal or permutation inference robust to counterfactual-model choice, but target sharp-null or prediction-style inference rather than selected symmetric ATT Wald coverage.
Chernozhukov, Wüthrich, and Zhu (2026, JPE, arXiv:1812.10820) use cross-fitting, debiasing, and self-normalized statistics for average SC effects, not a proximal role-selection frontier.
Leeb and Pötscher (2005) establish local nonuniformity of naive post-selection inference; Lee et al. (2016, arXiv:1311.6238) show how Gaussian selection geometry yields exact conditional pivots.
Lunde (2019, arXiv:1902.07425) proves dependent-data sample-splitting validity under beta-mixing with separated blocks, supplying the closest early-role/late-estimation machinery.
Andrews (1991) and Zhang and Wu (2017, arXiv:1508.07036) supply HAC and dependent Gaussian approximation tools, but do not resolve selector conditioning with singular stacked proximal covariances.
